blocks.text: Acts 12 narrates a period of persecution under Herod directed against the Jerusalem church. The chapter reports the execution of James and the arrest and miraculous deliverance of Peter. The time setting is the Feast of Unleavened Bread, following Passover. While the supplied evidence bundle contains archaeological materials from this period and location, the available evidence is primarily limited to ossuaries and inscriptional records rather than direct documentation of the events described in the narrative.
